objects.docstring:
poetry-island: a bounded client mount inside server-rendered HTML, the
one place in a Poetry page where the client owns the state. The server
renders a shell; the island's module, any file the importmap serves
that exports mount(element, props), mounts beside it on connect and
unmounts on disconnect. One controller handles the Turbo lifecycle for
every island: a morph refresh keeps the island and hands it the new
props, a cached snapshot's dead root is cleared, a preview shows the
shell, a failed import leaves the shell. State that must outlive the
page leaves through a form field rendered inside the island.

objects.docstring:
The Rails engine: component autoload paths, the controllers manifest,
previews, asset paths and the importmap pins. Loading the gem is the
only integration step besides `poetry:install`, which registers the
controller and pins the app's own islands directory.

A bounded client mount inside server-rendered HTML: the one place in
a Poetry page where the client owns the state, for a widget that
changes it many times a second (an editor, a canvas, a map, a 3D
scene). The block is the shell, what the page shows before the
module mounts and whenever it cannot. The module, an importmap
specifier exporting mount(element, props), mounts beside the shell
when the island connects and unmounts when it disconnects; a morph
refresh keeps the island and hands it the server's new props. State
that must outlive the page leaves through the form: name: renders a
hidden input inside the island for the module to write to.

examples.title: A map that paints the shell's box
examples.text:
<%= poetry_island(import: "islands/map", props: { center: [lat, lng] }, class: "h-80") do %>
  <%= image_tag "office-map.png", alt: "The office, on a map" %>
<% end %>

examples.title: An editor that takes the shell's place and submits with the form
examples.text:
<%= poetry_island(import: "islands/editor", mode: :flow, name: "post[body]", value: @post.body) do %>
  <%= sanitize(@post.body) %>
<% end %>

objects.docstring:
The island's classes: a positioned box for the root a fill island
paints, and a shell that steps aside once the island is up (the
controller marks the island data-island-mounted), keeping its box
under a fill island and leaving the flow under a flow one.
